Status: Active — resting at an Alpine Mountain Inn near Mighdural/Regal Capital after escaping the Planar Sanctum, meeting the Toad God, and discovering Thornbury's betrayal

Bones is a master infiltrator who survived Aegis Command, Order 120, and custody in the Corvinarus Planar Sanctum. After awakening alone in the Fractured Sanctum, Bones stole Fundamentals of Abjuration, uncovered Corvinarus's 10-page masterwork Veins of the Tapestry, refused the Oracle's flesh vat, engaged a fiendish Canoloth, was saved by the Toad God at the Astral Altar, and was teleported to the Regal Capital. There, at Alpine Bank, Bones eavesdropped on Thornbury placing a bounty on Archie Miser over a broken rope and claiming Legion credentials. Bones fled into a severe snowstorm and paid 3 Midland Ducats for shelter at an Alpine Inn.

The Pink Apocalypse — Dreamland (resident), Star Warriors (legacy), The Universe (maintenance)

Status: Active — goes wherever reality creaks loudest

Kirby is a pink spherical entity who lives in Dreamland and solves problems by eating them. This sounds simple until you realize the 'problems' Kirby eats include cosmic horrors, dimension-threatening nightmares, and beings that have destroyed galaxies. Kirby has saved existence multiple times while looking like a stress ball with feet. Waluigi has complicated feelings about Kirby because Waluigi respects EFFECTIVENESS, and Kirby is the most effective problem-solver Waluigi has ever encountered. Also, Kirby is TERRIFYING in ways that the cute exterior completely fails to communicate.

Evidence

  • Inhale — “Waluigi will list what Kirby can do, and readers should understand that this list is INCOMPLETE because nobody has found Kirby's limits: Inhale — Kirby can inhale virtually anything and either swallow it (destroying it)”
  • Copy Ability — “Copy Abilities — When Kirby swallows something with a distinct power, Kirby gains that power.”
  • Warp Star — “The Warp Star takes Kirby to where Kirby needs to be.”
  • Not the Whole Story — “Waluigi will list what Kirby can do, and readers should understand that this list is INCOMPLETE because nobody has found Kirby's limits: Inhale — Kirby can inhale virtually anything and either swallow it (destroying it)”

When Kirby swallows a creature or object with a distinct power (fire, blade, lightning, stone, ice, and so on) he spits it out and gains a copy of that power until he takes it off or uses Inhale again: one attack or trait of the GM's choosing, usually better than the original.

Status: Active — last confirmed location: the Shadowfell grove, where a massive fireball was hurled at Mazebounds

Bryan is the servant of a deity he calls the Toad God, and he arrived at Raventree's extended crisis with the mission-oriented certainty of someone who has received divine instruction and the practical limitations of someone who has never actually been to the Shadowfell. He recruited Dan from the Mages' Guild barracks, partnered with Mystic Morel for planar transit, and entered the Shadowfell hunting Archie Miser under a theological mandate that he described as being 'for the good of the world.' Waluigi notes that anyone hunting Archie Miser in the Shadowfell while carrying a mandate from a Toad God and traveling with a fortune-telling pickpocket is operating at a significant information disadvantage relative to the situation they have entered. Dracule Mihawk, known as the Hawk of Blackfen Pass, is a legendary swordsman and silent observer of the Old World's many crises. He stands as a pillar of stoic power, his golden eye glinting with the intensity of frozen fire. He reluctantly agreed to accompany a lone Iron Legion agent into the heart of Mount Ebott after recognizing the sigil of a division that was supposedly wiped out nearly a century ago. He prefers improvisation over outdated military protocol and remains highly skeptical of the agent's 'survey' mission.

Mr. L is either Luigi's darkest chapter or Luigi's truest self, depending on who you ask and how much you trust the official narrative. The Regency claims Mr. L was a temporary condition—Luigi brainwashed by dimensional forces, used as a weapon against the Mushroom Kingdom, eventually freed and returned to normal. The warrant charging Luigi with 'residual Mr. L activities' suggests the Regency does not fully believe their own story. The Loyalists claim Mr. L proves Luigi was always compromised and should never be trusted. Luigi himself went SILENT when asked if Mr. L did something evil—a silence witnessed by multiple parties at the ruined manor convergence. Waluigi has spent considerable effort investigating the Mr. L incident, and what Waluigi has found raises more questions than it answers. Was Luigi truly a puppet with someone else pulling the strings? Was Mr. L a separate personality that emerged under stress? Was the 'brainwashing' actually an AWAKENING of something that was always present? And most disturbingly—does Mr. L's existence connect to Mario's disappearance in ways that no one wants to acknowledge? Waluigi does not know. Waluigi is not sure anyone knows. But Waluigi is going to document every theory, every fragment of evidence, and every disturbing implication until the truth emerges or Waluigi runs out of paper. WAH.

Mystic Morel—also known as Purple T, also known as the singing Toad who robbed Archie Miser while he was pinned to a bed—is a purple Toad fortune teller who speaks in rhyming prophecies, performs full musical numbers during critical moments, pickpockets people while they're injured, opens planar portals using stolen equipment, and distributes magical tarot cards that depict events the recipient has not yet experienced. He carries divination incense that enhances prophecy. He is simultaneously the most annoying, the most mysterious, and possibly the most dangerous Toad Waluigi has ever encountered. WAH. Mystic Morel's file now includes direct confirmation that he was at the master-bedroom portal circle with Tanukiburt and the injured real Toadburt while the party held all four portal artifacts. This is exactly the sort of theatrical timing Waluigi expects from Purple T and exactly the sort of timing Waluigi hates. Someone killed Princess Peach on Highsun 1, 955 BF. That person's identity remains the central mystery of the assassination—the question that eighty-five years of investigation, propaganda, and civil war have failed to answer. The official narrative blamed Bowser, but the evidence is weak and Bowser has denied involvement consistently. Lady Bloomia's testimony claims the killer's identity is recorded in Princess Peach's list—'someone the Princess loved,' in the third column headed 'HELD THE BLADE.' Waluigi has encountered numerous theories about the assassin's identity. None are proven. All are disturbing in different ways. WAH.

Status: Active — minor landed knight-commander at Vellanet Rise; Regal Lion second-in-command on detached service; unaware his brother Archie is missing

Jack Melvus Miser is the eldest of the five Miser children and the reason the rest of them eat well. A paladin of the Oath of Glory who joined the Regal Lion at fifteen, he ground his way up from squire to the order's second-in-command on bandit cordons, unpriceable monster contracts, and one daylight kill on a rampaging Fire Elemental Myrmidon in front of a whole market town. He now holds Vellanet Rise — a minor Midlands-periphery grant of a fortified manor, three villages, a mill and a quarry — and leads his own body of arms, the Order of Jack, whose famous 20,000 is a muster roll rather than an army. Locally he is a hero; a hundred miles away he is nobody. He lifted his mother Wanda and his siblings out of poverty exactly as he said he would at fifteen, and has not yet been told that the brother missing from the family portrait is wanted across three planes.

From Leashed Agent to Indentured Archivist — Formerly Iron Legion (coerced), currently Shadow Estate Archives (indentured)

Status: Active — real injured Toadburt confirmed alive at the Shadow Estate portal circle with Tanukiburt and Mystic Morel

Toadburt's story is a masterclass in trading one cage for another. The Iron Legion strapped an entropy ring on him and sent him into the Feywild as a coerced operative. Now the ring is off, but Toadburt isn't free—he's working for the Shadow Estate's Archivist in exchange for gradual healing, recovering from his injuries over two-week intervals while organizing books in a vampire library. Waluigi recognizes this pattern: someone too damaged to refuse help, accepting terms from whoever offers it, trading independence for survival. It's not slavery. It's not freedom. It's the grey area in between that nobody likes to name. The Toadburt question has changed from unresolved suspicion to immediate rescue problem. Remi's exterior scouting confirmed an injured real Toadburt gathered at the master-bedroom portal circle with Tanukiburt and Mystic Morel while the rug was being covered and uncovered. This means Toadburt is alive, not free, and positioned at the exact route the party needs to use.

The Quartermaster Spy Who Itemized The Apocalypse — Mages' Guild

Status: Active — operating with the Mages' Guild, recently ear-dragged, still tracking receipts somehow

Thornbury is a stuffy, penny-pinching Mages' Guild operative who charged Archie 2,000 gold for a broken rope. He later brought Archie and Bones rubber duckies for a bubble bath, only to be dragged away by the ear by a disgruntled noblewoman. He left behind a notebook proving he was spying on the party the entire time. Waluigi has zero respect for a spy who is defeated by a bath time interruption. Thornbury is the Mages' Guild operative who proves that evil does not always arrive with a death ray, a monologue, or even decent posture. Sometimes evil arrives with a ledger, a rope, and a reimbursement policy. He accompanied Agent L, Luigi, and Archie through the ruined manor while secretly gathering intelligence on the party, cataloguing environmental anomalies, pocketing suspicious rings, uncovering hidden stashes, and charging Archie 2,062 gold pieces and 5 silver for breaking a single rope. He is a field spy, quartermaster, scavenger, emergency supplier, expense auditor, and apparently a man who believes no supernatural catastrophe is too urgent for itemized billing. He brought practical supplies to dangerous situations, helped navigate the manor, provided rope, potions, a Sending scroll, and a tensor box, and then managed to undermine all professional credibility by getting caught taking a heated luxury bath while soldiers suffered outside. Byscilla Danos dragged him away by the ear like an embarrassing child, and in his haste he left behind field notes proving he had been spying on everyone the entire time. Waluigi despises nearly everything about Thornbury on principle. Unfortunately, historical accuracy requires admitting that the man is actually COMPETENT, which is infuriating. WAH.

The Dead Man Who Took His Secrets With Him — Mages' Guild (Senior Enforcer)

Status: Deceased — killed by Archie Miser in a public market, 1040 BF. Ruled 'justifiable magical defense' by Onyx Hand tribunal.

Valorian Stormweave was a Senior Enforcer of the Mages' Guild who—according to Lady Bloomia's testimony—was present at the Royal Vault on the morning of Princess Peach's assassination in 955 BF. He allegedly delayed the Solstice Crown delivery, knew Bloomia's name without introduction, smiled 'like a predator who has confirmed the location of its prey,' and was part of the Guild's involvement in 'the arrangement.' He lived for eighty-five years after allegedly helping murder a princess. Then Archie Miser killed him in a public market during an altercation that an Onyx Hand tribunal ruled justifiable. The only person who could have testified about Guild complicity in the assassination is now ash. Whether this is cosmic justice, cosmic irony, or cosmic convenience depends entirely on who you ask—and EVERYONE has an opinion. Waluigi has spent considerable time examining this death because it sits at the intersection of two stories that should have nothing to do with each other: Archie's chaotic journey and the eighty-five-year-old assassination conspiracy. The intersection is either coincidence or something much worse. WAH.

Chancellor Toadsworth is the current head of the Mushroom Regency and the son of Toadsworth the Elder—the man whose journals allegedly confess to enabling Princess Peach's assassination. The Chancellor has spent his career maintaining the Regency's official narrative, suppressing investigation leads, and continuing relationships with the Mages' Guild and Iron Legion—both implicated in various aspects of the assassination and its aftermath. Captain Toadette's Loyalists recently placed him under house arrest. What they extract from him—through interrogation, coercion, or whatever methods Toadette considers appropriate—may finally answer questions that have haunted the kingdom for generations. Waluigi is not optimistic that the truth will emerge cleanly. WAH.

The Plumber Who Vanished — Mushroom Kingdom (Former Hero) / Unknown

Status: Missing — Presumed alive, location unknown, last confirmed sighting 1039 BF at the Star Fountain

Mario is—or WAS—the most famous hero in the Mushroom Kingdom. The man who saved Princess Peach countless times before her assassination in 955 BF. The red-capped plumber who could jump higher than physics should allow, who stomped Bowser's schemes into the ground repeatedly, who was so synonymous with heroism that his NAME became a verb. And then, after eighty-five years of diminished appearances and growing silence, he DISAPPEARED entirely. Luigi found him at the Star Fountain. They flew together on wing caps. Luigi said 'Nothing can hurt us... as long as we're together.' And then Mario was GONE again, and Luigi is working alone for the Mages' Guild at Raventree Manor, sucking up ghosts with a vacuum cleaner and refusing to explain ANYTHING. Waluigi has spent considerable effort piecing together what happened. The picture that emerges is worse than a simple disappearance. WAH. The Garden Above the Fire does not return Mario; it makes his absence louder, because Luigi's rescue ends with Luigi asking the brother who is not in the room whether they are still superstars.

The Ghost Researcher Who Disappeared — Formerly Mushroom Kingdom Royal Science Division / Formerly Boo Research Institute / Formerly Gadd Science Incorporated (dissolved) / Rumored connections to entities Waluigi cannot confirm

Status: Unknown — last confirmed public appearance approximately 1028 BF, current location classified or unknown

Professor Elvin Gadd — known publicly as E. Gadd — was the Mushroom Kingdom's foremost expert on paranormal phenomena, spectral containment, dimensional engineering, and what academic literature delicately calls 'paratechnological development.' He invented the Poltergust, the device Luigi uses to capture ghosts. He invented the Pixelator, a matter-to-data conversion system whose applications remain classified. He invented the Ghost Portrificationizer, the Dark-Light Device, the Dual Scream communicator, and at minimum twenty-three other devices that Waluigi has found references to in fragmentary documentation — most of which are described only by codename and clearance level. He served the Mushroom Kingdom's royal family for over seven decades in various advisory capacities. He trained Luigi personally in ghost-hunting operations. He was present — in some capacity that records do not specify — during multiple events that shaped the kingdom's recent history. And then, approximately twelve years ago, Professor E. Gadd stopped appearing in public. His laboratories were seized by government authority. His research was classified. His name was removed from active academic registries. His former colleagues were discouraged from discussing him. His correspondence was returned unopened. The official explanation is 'retirement to pursue private research.' The unofficial explanation varies depending on who Waluigi asks — some say he discovered something too dangerous to publish, some say he was silenced by parties unknown, some say he simply got tired of institutional politics and walked away. Waluigi has attempted to locate Professor E. Gadd for interview purposes. Waluigi has been unsuccessful. This is unusual, because Waluigi is very good at finding people who do not want to be found. E. Gadd is either dead, dimensionally displaced, or being protected by resources that exceed Waluigi's investigative capabilities. Waluigi does not know which. Waluigi would very much like to find out. WAH.

Mistveil is one of Captain Toadette's most effective intelligence operatives—a specialist in infiltration, extraction, and the acquisition of secrets that powerful people prefer to keep hidden. At Fawful's gala, Mistveil posed as a minor noble and extracted Chief Thornpaw's confirmation of his relationship with Princess Peach—testimony that validated decades of Loyalist theories. Waluigi respects professional excellence even when it serves factions whose methods disturb him. Mistveil is professionally excellent. Mistveil is also absolutely dedicated to Captain Toadette's vision, which means Mistveil is DANGEROUS in ways that go beyond mere competence. WAH.

The King Who Held the Door — Koopa Troop (King) / Disaster Inc. (current situation)

Status: Active — operating in the Shadow Estate; carrying necromantic evidence; royal war chest active; illegal under hostile mandates and still completely unbothered

Bowser is the King of the Koopa Troop, a giant fire-breathing turtle-dragon who was cast into the Shadowfell during the Planar Fracture alongside Archie Miser. Since then, he has attended a vampire dinner party where he presumably sat wherever he wanted, tackled a vampire lord through a gothic window, bit a giant bat's wing, and most recently held a door shut against an axe-wielding succession claimant while Markop was unconscious—then punched said claimant in the head and picked up a necromancer's wand asking 'Is this a magic wand?' with the innocent curiosity of a child finding a toy. Waluigi has arm-wrestled Bowser and LOST. Waluigi has also competed against Bowser in every sport imaginable. Bowser is not complicated. Bowser is EFFECTIVE. The current party pass identifies Bowser as Disaster Inc.'s blunt-force sovereign: door-holder, threat magnet, and walking siege engine whose honesty remains more reliable than most alliances.

The Plumber Who Vanished — Mushroom Kingdom (Former Hero) / Unknown

Status: Missing — Presumed alive, location unknown, last confirmed sighting 1039 BF at the Star Fountain

Mario is—or WAS—the most famous hero in the Mushroom Kingdom. The man who saved Princess Peach countless times before her assassination in 955 BF. The red-capped plumber who could jump higher than physics should allow, who stomped Bowser's schemes into the ground repeatedly, who was so synonymous with heroism that his NAME became a verb. And then, after eighty-five years of diminished appearances and growing silence, he DISAPPEARED entirely. Luigi found him at the Star Fountain. They flew together on wing caps. Luigi said 'Nothing can hurt us... as long as we're together.' And then Mario was GONE again, and Luigi is working alone for the Mages' Guild at Raventree Manor, sucking up ghosts with a vacuum cleaner and refusing to explain ANYTHING. Waluigi has spent considerable effort piecing together what happened. The picture that emerges is worse than a simple disappearance. WAH. The Garden Above the Fire does not return Mario; it makes his absence louder, because Luigi's rescue ends with Luigi asking the brother who is not in the room whether they are still superstars.

The Rakasha Who Loved a Princess — Rakasha Tribes (Chief)

Status: Active — still leading his people after eighty-five years, which raises questions about Rakasha lifespans

Chief Thornpaw is the leader of the Rakasha and—according to his own testimony at Fawful's gala—was involved in a secret relationship with Princess Peach before her assassination. He claims to have been shown the secret hatch in her chambers, to have visited her privately through that passage, and to have fathered a child with her. If his testimony is accurate, he is one of the most important witnesses to the events surrounding the assassination. If his testimony is fabricated or manipulated, he may be something else entirely—a plant, a patsy, or a participant in whatever actually happened. Waluigi has learned to be careful about accepting testimony at face value, even testimony that seems emotionally authentic. Especially testimony that seems emotionally authentic. Grief can be performed. Love can be invented. And Thornpaw has had eighty-five years to construct whatever narrative serves his purposes. WAH.

The Smallest Rattle — Snowdin Household

Status: Active — recorded in the Snowdin household registry

The youngest bone in the house, a fearless little skeleton whose rattling steps can interrupt even the most solemn family meeting. Baby Bones treats every adult as a potential carrier and every puzzle piece as a toy. The household treats them as a promise to build something gentler than the world it inherited.

Evidence

  • Bite — “Lunch is attended seriously, in the high seat, with a plate and a napkin and the ceremonial first bite that Papyrus narrates like a state occasion.”
  • Keen Records — “Sans, told afterward, was quiet for a long time and then said, 'good ears,' in a tone the chronicle describes, unusually, as proud and unsettled in equal measure.”
  • Mechanical Aptitude — “Morning begins with a demand for transport, granted by whichever adult is nearest, and a tour of the house at shoulder height, during which every object is inspected, several are confiscated, and one — today, a spoon”
  • Puzzle Discipline — “Baby Bones treats every adult as a potential carrier and every puzzle piece as a toy.”

The Smiley Trashbag — Snowdin Recycling Crew

Status: Active — recorded in the Snowdin household registry

A bag-wrapped brother who salvages bent puzzle parts, cracked toys, and almost-useful cookware. Baby Bones's favorite rattle and Papyrus's emergency spaghetti strainer both came from his workbench. He dislikes the nickname, but accepts it because it reminds Snowdin that discarded does not mean worthless.

Evidence

  • Club — “The Smiley Trashbag”
  • Keen Records — “The chronicle has verified, with a small and growing unease, that the rubble he describes salvaging from was, before the war, a storage site no record connects to anything.”
  • Mechanical Aptitude — “In the thin years after the war, when Snowdin was rebuilding from what it could scavenge, a puzzle mechanism from the old corridor came out of the rubble bent beyond any official repair schedule — the town's assessors”
  • Unsettling Insight — “The household finds this either hoarding or prophecy, and the record keeps siding with prophecy at inconvenient intervals.”

Status: Active — recorded in the Snowdin household registry

A purple-clad cousin who announces every entrance as though it were the last act of an opera. His “very special attack” is a family legend with so many versions that nobody agrees whether it is a spell, a dance, or an exceptionally difficult puzzle. Papyrus encourages him; Sans keeps a safe distance when the announcements begin.

A pale figure in black whose relationship to the family is documented only by sightings, sketches, and absence. Mysteryman appears near sealed rooms, broken save points, and old photographs. The household policy is simple: leave a seat, ask no cruel questions, and do not pretend an unfinished person is erased.

Hired Off a Noticeboard — Wario's Enterprise (casual labour, one expedition, agreed share of proceeds: none)

Status: Last seen 18 Aethel 1032 BF aboard the Wariocopter, scalp wound from the crash still unpaid, heading aft for food after the All Clear. He was nearly twenty-three. The One-T file continues.

Jory Dobbs answered an advertisement for skilled labour, sat through a briefing at which a chair fell over and a vase was destroyed, was offered no share of the treasure whatsoever, pocketed a forged passport in lieu of wages, and found himself in a taped-together charter flying into a storm with a man in a produce sack. He took a bracket to the head in the crash, bled down one side of his face for the rest of the day, tied every knot in the rope chain correctly, and was the first person to say out loud that they had climbed the wrong mountain.
